newsitem.title: MEXICO: Inbursa targets three pct pension share.
newsitem.headline: Inbursa targets three pct pension share.

text.p: Banco Inbursa, the banking unit of Grupo Financiero Inbursa, is targetting a three percent share of the Mexican pension market and is not contemplating taking on a partner, a top official said on Thursday.

"We're hoping to administer recourses of two to three percent of the new Mexican pensions market, we have a conservative figure because we're looking to provide top quality service and returns," Roberto Isaac Rodriguez, head of Inbursa's pension management firm, or Afore, told Reuters.

He said authorities were expected to notify Inbursa in early December whether its petition to set up an Afore had been accepted. The privately-run pension firms are due to start operating in mid-1997.

Inbursa plans to invest 50 million pesos in setting up the unit, about half of which is necessary for building reserves, he said. By law, each Afore must start up with at least 25 million pesos in capital.
Some $5 million will be put into developing systems to handle pension accounts, he added.

While many other banks are joining forces with foreign firms -- many with experience in other Latin American pension markets -- to enter the Mexican pension market, Inbursa plans to go in unaccompanied, Isaac Rodriguez said.
"The experience of Mexico is very special, we have to be very creative and we are going alone in setting up the Afore," he said.
